chunks: And by his chain, from Al-Halby who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who emancipated his concubine, is it correct for him that he marries her without a waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So others?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until she observes the waiting period of three months'.

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who copulated with his slave girl, is it correct for him that he marries her before she observes the waiting period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'How much is her waiting period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One menstruation or two'.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a man to marry his freed concubine or slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the distinct iddah periods for a master marrying his freed concubine (three months) versus his slave girl after intercourse (one or two menstruations), highlighting the juristic nuance between emancipation and continued slavery. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition's reliance on the Imam's precise definitions to resolve practical marital eligibility, distinguishing these cases from the general three-month iddah of divorce found in the Quran.
